quests.question: ___ happens in the negotiations, both sides have agreed to keep talking.
quests.hint: This word doubles as the subject of the verb right after it, and means 'no matter what'.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever' means 'no matter what' and also functions as the subject of 'happens' — the other options cannot serve as a subject this way.

quests.question: ___ that public opinion was divided, the government pressed ahead with the reform.
quests.hint: This very formal phrase introduces a concession, suited to official writing.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite divided opinion, the reform proceeded.

quests.question: The bill was withdrawn ___ it lacked sufficient support in parliament.
quests.hint: A lack of support explains the withdrawal.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — insufficient support caused the withdrawal.

quests.question: Exhausted ___ she was, she refused to stop until the report was finished.
quests.hint: This word can directly follow a fronted adjective — its closest relative usually cannot fit this exact pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Though' fits this fronted-adjective pattern; 'although' is not used this way in standard modern English.

quests.question: The forecast is useful ___ it accounts for seasonal demand shifts.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the forecast's usefulness extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the usefulness is limited to this specific factor.

quests.question: The quarterly numbers were disappointing, ___ leadership remained confident about the year ahead.
quests.hint: Weak short-term results didn't shake overall confidence.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — disappointing numbers didn't change leadership's outlook.

quests.question: ___ wins the election will inherit a growing budget deficit.
quests.hint: This word doubles as the subject of the verb right after it, and means 'no matter who'.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'no matter who' and also functions as the subject of 'wins' — the other options cannot serve as a subject this way.

quests.question: The current policy rewards short-term results, ___ the proposed one favors long-term investment.
quests.hint: Two policies are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two policies with two different priorities.

quests.question: ___ competitors are already using automation, the company can't afford to fall behind.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for a strategic urgency.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — competitor automation justifies the urgency.

quests.question: The two proposals are nearly identical, ___ the second includes a longer trial period.
quests.hint: This phrase works like 'except that', pointing out the single difference.
quests.explanation: 'Save that' means 'except that' — it introduces the single specific difference between two otherwise similar proposals.

quests.question: The model holds true ___ market conditions remain relatively stable.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the model holds true.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — the model's accuracy depends on this specific condition.

quests.question: The paper was widely discussed ___ it challenged a long-accepted assumption.
quests.hint: A bold claim explains the wide discussion.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — challenging an assumption caused the wide discussion.

quests.question: ___ the conference is held next year, attendance is expected to set a new record.
quests.hint: This word means 'no matter where' and introduces a place, regardless of which one.
quests.explanation: 'Wherever' means 'no matter where' — the location doesn't change the expected record attendance.

quests.question: ___ did the study challenge earlier findings, but it also proposed an entirely new model.
quests.hint: This correlative opener uniquely triggers a moved helper verb right after it.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' at the front of a sentence triggers inversion — the other options never trigger this word order.

quests.question: The earlier model assumed constant growth, ___ the revised one accounts for seasonal variation.
quests.hint: Two models are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two models built on two different assumptions.

quests.question: ___ difficult the climb becomes, the guides always ensure everyone's safety.
quests.hint: This word means 'no matter how' when placed directly before an adjective.
quests.explanation: Before an adjective, 'however' can mean 'no matter how' — a distinct subordinating use, separate from the semicolon-linking adverb.

quests.question: ___ that the new regulations increased costs, most operators supported the change.
quests.hint: This formal phrase signals a concession — a fact that doesn't change the outcome — in official writing.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite higher costs, most operators still supported it.

quests.question: Operators can comply within six months, ___ they can apply for a limited extension.
quests.hint: Two options are offered — only one path will be taken.
quests.explanation: 'Or' presents two alternatives — either meeting the deadline or requesting an extension.

quests.question: ___ option the board chooses, shareholders expect a clear explanation.
quests.hint: This word means 'no matter which', introducing a choice among specific options.
quests.explanation: 'Whichever' means 'no matter which' — regardless of the specific option chosen, an explanation is expected.

quests.question: The precedent applies ___ the facts of the new case closely resemble the original ruling.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the precedent applies.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the precedent's reach is limited to this specific similarity.

quests.question: The appeal was dismissed ___ no new evidence had been presented.
quests.hint: A lack of new material explains the dismissal.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — the absence of new evidence caused the dismissal.

quests.question: The report contained no factual errors, ___ did it omit any relevant data.
quests.hint: This word continues a negative idea and requires the subject and helper verb to swap places.
quests.explanation: 'Nor' continues a negative statement and triggers inversion — 'did it omit' swaps the normal word order, unlike 'because/so/although'.

quests.question: The original statute focused narrowly on fraud, ___ the amendment covers a much broader range of offenses.
quests.hint: Two versions of the same law are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two versions with two different scopes.

quests.question: ___ the defendant had no prior record, the judge imposed a lighter sentence.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for a judicial decision.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — the clean record justified the lighter sentence.

quests.question: Skeptical ___ he was, the investor still agreed to hear the full proposal.
quests.hint: This word can directly follow a fronted adjective — its closest relative usually cannot fit this exact pattern.
quests.explanation: This inverted adjective-first pattern calls specifically for 'though' — 'although' doesn't slot into this structure.

quests.question: The partnership benefits both companies ___ shared resources reduce overall costs.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the partnership's benefit extends.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — the benefit is measured specifically by reduced costs.

quests.question: The pitch had obvious flaws, ___ three investors offered funding on the spot.
quests.hint: Noticeable weaknesses didn't stop a strong response.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' shows surprising contrast — flaws in the pitch didn't prevent quick funding offers.

quests.question: ___ the committee ultimately decides, the process itself has already improved transparency.
quests.hint: This word doubles as part of the clause right after it, and means 'no matter what'.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever' means 'no matter what' — regardless of the committee's conclusion, the process has already improved transparency.

quests.question: ___ that the deadline was extended, most teams submitted their work early anyway.
quests.hint: Common in official documents, this phrase concedes a point without changing the outcome.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite the extension, most teams still submitted early.

quests.question: The response was ___ an overwhelming success that organizers doubled the venue size for next year.
quests.hint: Unlike its close relative, this word needs a noun phrase directly after it.
quests.explanation: 'Such' combines with a noun phrase before 'that' — the overwhelming response explains the doubled venue.
